title: Reporting Line Common Manager

statement.md: A firm has $n$ people numbered $1$ to $n$. Person $1$ is the head. Every other person $i$ has exactly one direct manager $p_i$, and following managers always ends at person $1$.
For each query $(u, v)$ print the **lowest common manager**: the deepest person who is $u$, $v$, or a manager of both (a person counts as their own manager here).

inputFormat: First line: $n$ and $q$. Second line: $n - 1$ integers, the managers of persons $2, 3, \dots, n$ (empty if $n = 1$). Then $q$ lines `u v`.
constraints: Manager numbers are not necessarily smaller than the person number
The tree can be a chain of length $10^5$
hints: Walking up from both nodes one step at a time costs the tree depth, up to $n$ per query.
Precompute the $2^k$-th ancestor of every node, and first lift the deeper node to the depth of the other.
editorial: [{"type": "p", "md": "Compute depths with an iterative traversal from the root (a recursive one can overflow on a chain). Build `up[k][v]`, the $2^k$-th ancestor of $v$. For a query lift the deeper node by the depth difference, return it if the two meet, otherwise lift both together from the largest $k$ down while their ancestors differ, and the answer is the parent. Preprocessing is $O(n \\log n)$ and each query $O(\\log n)$."}]
